model_annotation: The plot shows multiple line series intended to illustrate how a single measured metric (y-axis) changes as a function of an x-axis parameter for several methods listed in the legend (FT, IKE, MEMIT, and ROME), with two additional unlabeled series also drawn. The x-axis has no visible label in the provided image, uses a linear scale, and displays tick labels at approximately 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 (regularly spaced at 0.1 intervals), with the plotted points spanning roughly from just below 0.1 (leftmost points) to just above 0.3 (rightmost points). The y-axis label and numeric tick labels are not visible/legible in the provided image; the axis appears linear with evenly spaced horizontal gridlines, but the exact value range and tick interval cannot be read. The FT series is drawn as a blue solid line with downward-pointing triangle markers and rises steadily from the leftmost to the rightmost point. The IKE series is a red solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers and also increases steadily across the x-range. The MEMIT series is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers and increases across x, with a relatively larger jump between the first and second points and smaller increments thereafter. The ROME series is a green solid line with square markers and increases across x, with its rightmost point reaching the top edge of the plotting area (clipped at the upper boundary). In addition, there is a black solid line with circular markers that increases from the first through the third point and then appears approximately flat between the third and fourth points, and a brown solid line with diamond markers that increases across x with a noticeable rise between the second and third points and continues upward to the final point.
